RFC7854-3.2-1.note: nextReconnectWait doubles and caps at reconnectMax; a refused dial is not retried before the base wait even when the port reopens early

RFC7854-3.2-2.note: after the collector closes a session the sender reconnects, and not before the base wait since the first session

RFC7854-3.3-1.note: after reconnect Peer Up precedes the surviving route and each family gets EOR after its routes; an incremental UPDATE and another collector's reconnect produce no EOR, and an incomplete snapshot never emits EOR

RFC7854-4.1-1.note: type 200 is skipped and the following Termination is consumed; a malformed Peer Up still ends the session

RFC7854-4.10-1.note: First verdict 2026-09-29. The row's sentence is the lead-in to the §4.10 figure, the only statement of the Peer Up layout, so the obligation judged is that figure: Local Address (16), Local Port, Remote Port, Sent OPEN, Received OPEN after the per-peer header (Information TLVs are RFC7854-x-19, the OPEN contents RFC7854-x-8). Positive rfc7854_message_layout_test.go::TestRFC7854PeerUpIsThePerPeerHeaderThenTheFixedFieldsAndBothOPENs reads each field raw at its offset from writePeerUp output and the exact total length. Negative ::TestRFC7854PeerUpShorterThanItsFixedFieldsIsRefused: a valid Peer Up is accepted, the same cut 10 octets into the fixed fields is refused (decodePeerUp short check).

RFC7854-4.2-1.note: transmitted Route Monitoring on both directions has reserved bits 0; a Peer Up with every reserved bit set is accepted and its defined flags decode unchanged

RFC7854-4.3-2.note: First verdict 2026-09-29. Positive rfc7854_message_layout_test.go::TestRFC7854InitiationIsTheCommonHeaderThenTwoOrMoreTLVs reads the octets sender.go::sendInitiation writes off a pipe, checks type 4 and walks TLVs by hand from octet 6 to exactly the end, requiring >= 2. Negative (R1(a)) ::TestRFC7854InitiationWithFewerThanTwoTLVsIsRefused: a one-TLV Initiation is refused by the receiver. The refusal comes from decodeInitiation's sysName-presence check (RFC7854-x-18), not a count check, but every one-TLV Initiation lacks sysName or sysDescr, so no one-TLV input is accepted; the buffer is otherwise valid.

RFC7854-4.4-1.note: Initiation and Peer Up strings reach the command output in transmitted order, with duplicates kept

RFC7854-4.4-2.note: sysDescr carries the running build and uname sysname, release and machine, the MIB-II sysDescr content; it changes when the build identity changes

RFC7854-4.4-3.note: sysName is the configured host.domain FQDN, the MIB-II sysName convention, survives rollback, and follows a configuration change

RFC7854-4.5-1.note: after stop() the collector reads the Termination then EOF; a Peer Up afterwards is refused with errNotConnected

RFC7854-4.5-2.note: receiver closes after reading a Termination with the router end held open (well under the read deadline) and drops the router; without a Termination two valid messages leave the session open

RFC7854-4.5-3.note: live shutdown Termination carries exactly one two-octet Reason; absent, empty, short and long Reason TLVs fail decode and end the session

RFC7854-4.5-4.note: First verdict 2026-09-29. Positive rfc7854_message_layout_test.go::TestRFC7854TerminationIsTheCommonHeaderThenTLVs reads the octets the sender's Termination path writes, walks TLVs from octet 6 to exactly the end, requires at least one and exactly one Reason TLV. Negative ::TestRFC7854TerminationWithNoTLVIsRefused: a 6-octet header-only Termination is refused (decodeTermination's missing-Reason branch, which any zero-TLV body reaches).

RFC7854-4.5-5.note: Station clause: termination_absent_test.go::TestBMPReceiverEndsTheSessionWhenTheRouterLeavesWithoutTermination sends Initiation + Peer Up, confirms one router and one peer held, closes the pipe with no Termination, and requires handleSession to return with zero routers and zero peers (record: removeRouter break observed red). RECOMMENDED clause: sender_queue_test.go::TestSenderStopSendsTerminationToCollector reads a Termination on the collector side through stop() racing holdConnection (record: writeTerminationLocked break observed red). {single-polarity: positive} holds: the sentence permits the no-message close, so no non-compliant router input exists for the station to refuse.

RFC7854-4.7-1.note: transmitted Route Mirroring ends with the BGP Message TLV; Information then BGP Message is accepted, BGP Message then Information ends the session

RFC7854-4.7-2.note: Errored PDU with a BGP Message TLV is accepted; Errored PDU without one ends the session

RFC7854-4.7-3.note: First verdict 2026-09-29. Positive rfc7854_message_layout_test.go::TestRFC7854RouteMirroringIsThePerPeerHeaderThenTLVs: writeRouteMirroring output decodes a per-peer header equal to the input at octet 6, then TLVs walked by hand from octet 48 to exactly the end, same types and values in order. Negative ::TestRFC7854RouteMirroringWhoseBodyIsNotTLVsIsRefused: the valid message is first accepted, then a 3-octet tail that is no TLV (length fixed up) is refused, so only the not-TLVs body differs.

RFC7854-4.8-1.note: unknown stat type 60000 and a 3-octet counter are consumed and the session survives; a stat length past the report end still ends it

RFC7854-4.8-2.note: a transmitted report carries one statistic; an empty report is refused before it reaches the collector

RFC7854-4.8-3.note: First verdict 2026-09-29. Positive rfc7854_message_layout_test.go::TestRFC7854StatsReportCountNamesTheCountersThatFollow: the 4-octet count at octet 48 equals 3 and exactly three counter TLVs, walked by hand, run to the end with the input types and values. Negative ::TestRFC7854StatsReportCountDisagreeingWithItsCountersIsRefused: the valid report is first accepted, then count+1 (truncated entry) and count-1 (trailing data) are each refused by decodeStatisticsReport.

RFC7854-4.9-1.note: reasons 1 and 3 carry the exact NOTIFICATION PDU and reason 5 carries no Data, but the reason 2 clause ('the code corresponding to the FSM Event that caused the system to close the session') is unproven: the producer writes the constant fsmEventNone for every reason 2, so the subtest's two-zero-octet assertion cannot fail on a wrong event code, and the subtest drives 'connection lost', an unexpected transport termination that Section 4.9 assigns to reason 4, not reason 2

RFC7854-5-1.note: Re-judged 2026-09-29 (the negative unit gained the RFC7854-5-4 tag line only; assertions unchanged). rfc7854_test.go::TestRFC7854LFlagFollowsPolicy: received announce and withdraw leave with L clear, sent with L set. ::TestRFC7854LFlagNotDecidedByBody: one body streamed on both sides leaves L clear received and L set sent, so the flag follows the direction (policy stage) and not the message. Ze sends no post-policy Adj-RIB-In; its L-set stream is the RFC 8671 Adj-RIB-Out (O and L set, peerHeaderFromEvent).

RFC7854-5-2.note: replayed routes and EORs with unknown receipt time carry 0.0; a known receipt time survives replay exactly

RFC7854-5-4.note: First verdict 2026-09-29 (first clause of the §5 sentence; the twice-sent-withdraw clause left with retired RFC7854-5-3). Producer peerHeaderFromEvent sets L only on the sent direction, so a route's announcement and its withdraw take their L from the same direction. Positive rfc7854_test.go::TestRFC7854LFlagFollowsPolicy: a received withdraw carries L clear like a received announce, a sent withdraw L set like a sent announce. Negative ::TestRFC7854LFlagNotDecidedByBody: the same withdraw body on both sides gets L clear and L set, so a withdraw cannot carry the other side's flag. Both observed red under the peerHeaderFromEvent break. The test does not pair one announce with its own withdraw by prefix; the direction is the only input L reads, so no pairing can diverge.

RFC7854-5-6.note: rfc7854_replay_test.go::TestRFC7854ChangedAttributesCanReturnToEarlierValue receives one prefix three times with ORIGIN IGP, INCOMPLETE, IGP and requires exactly three Route Monitoring messages, each body byte-equal to the UPDATE carrying that ORIGIN, so a sender that suppresses or dedupes the return to an earlier value fails (record: handleSenderUpdate break observed red). One attribute (ORIGIN) samples 'such as an attribute change'. {single-polarity: positive} holds: every route change is compliant input to the router, which has no refusal path.

RFC7854-8.2-1.note: Loc-RIB instance Peer Up carries ports 0/0; a BGP peer's Peer Up carries its real 179/40000

RFC7854-x-1.note: Re-judged 2026-09-29. rfc7854_wire_header_test.go::TestRFC7854EveryTransmittedMessageCarriesVersion3AndItsTotalLength builds all seven types through the writers the sender calls (writeRouteMonitoring, writeStatisticsReport, writePeerDown, writePeerUp, writeInitiation, writeTermination, writeRouteMirroring) into a 0xA5-patterned buffer and requires octet 0 == 3 on each, so a writer that emits another version or leaves the octet unset goes red. The sentence binds the sender and no input can make it send another version; the negatives (header_test decode table #2, session_test TestBMPMalformedHeaderDrops) are the receiver refusing a version-2 header, the same rule read at the other end. The old decode-table positive stays tagged and proves only decode.

RFC7854-x-10.note: TestBMPSenderPeerDown round-trips a Reason byte the caller chose (5), so it cannot fail on a wrong cause; TestHandleSenderStatePeerDown pins reason 2 ('no notification message was sent') for an event whose close reason is 'notification'. No unit ties a Reason to the cause that closed the session, and the producer peerDownFor (bmp_events.go) never emits reason 4, so an unexpected transport termination (which Section 4.9 assigns to reason 4) is reported as a local close

RFC7854-x-11.note: Re-judged 2026-09-29: the stale unit TestSenderStopSendsTerminationToCollector changed only by an added RFC7854-4.5-5 tag comment; body unchanged. It still requires the collector to read a Termination through stop() racing holdConnection, and the writeTerminationLocked break recorded under RFC7854-4.5-5 on this same unit was observed red. sender_test.go::TestBMPSenderTermination covers the encoder, no record. {single-polarity: positive} holds for a MAY that ze always exercises.

RFC7854-x-12.note: receiver loop driven with Initiation and Termination writes zero bytes toward the router end; single-polarity marker

RFC7854-x-15.note: statistics-timeout 1 through the reload rail yields two reports about one interval apart; statistics-timeout 0 yields none

RFC7854-x-16.note: Re-judged 2026-09-29. The wrong tags on TestConcurrentDumpsStayAddressedToTheirOwnCollector are gone. rfc7854_session_opening_test.go::TestRFC7854SessionPeerUpOnlyForEstablishedPeers primes a new collector (primeSender) over one Established peer and one peer that exchanged OPENs and sent an UPDATE but never reported Up; it counts Peer Ups per address on the collector's bytes: exactly 1 for the Established peer, 0 for the other, and the first message is the Peer Up. A producer that announced every peer with cached OPENs, or none, goes red.

RFC7854-x-17.note: Re-judged 2026-09-29. rfc7854_session_opening_test.go::TestRFC7854SessionDumpsAdjRIBInAfterThePeerUp reads the same two-peer session in order: no Route Monitoring before the Peer Up, the Established peer's received route (exact UPDATE body announceBody(1)) arrives as a pre-policy Route Monitoring (L clear, the default pre-policy selection), and nothing is dumped for the peer that never reached Established. Order, content and scope of the Adj-RIB-In dump are each asserted.

RFC7854-x-18.note: Re-judged 2026-09-29. Both clauses now hold both polarities. Sender: rfc7854_test.go TestRFC7854InitiationCarriesSysDescr and the new rfc7854_session_opening_test.go::TestRFC7854InitiationCarriesSysName decode the Initiation sendInitiation writes and require exactly one sysName (type 2) and a sysDescr (type 1). Receiver: TestRFC7854InitiationMissingSysDescrEndsSession and TestBMPInitiationMissingSysNameEndsSession (tag added) each send an Initiation missing one TLV and require the session closed (decodeInitiation checks each independently); TestRFC7854InitiationEmptyIdentityValuesAccepted keeps presence, not length, as the test.

RFC7854-x-2.note: Re-judged 2026-09-29. TestRFC7854EveryTransmittedMessageCarriesVersion3AndItsTotalLength reads the transmitted octets of all seven types: octet 0 == 3 (so never the reserved 0), octets 1-4 == the whole message computed independently from the case's own inputs (common header + per-peer header where present + data) and equal to the octets the writer produced, and octet 5 == the type. Each clause of the quoted definition is asserted on a sent message. The tagged negative (header_test, a 3-octet buffer refused) is thin, but the clauses are sender field definitions with no input to refuse; the positive discriminates every one.

RFC7854-x-3.note: Re-judged 2026-09-29. rfc7854_wire_header_test.go::TestRFC7854PerPeerHeaderFollowsTheCommonHeader writes all seven types and decodes a per-peer header at octet 6 of Route Monitoring, Statistics Report, Peer Down, Peer Up and Route Mirroring, requiring it to equal the header the writer was given (4-octet AS 4200000001); for Initiation and Termination it requires the first TLV (type 1, length 2) at octet 6 and a message too short to hold a per-peer header, which is the 'most' of the sentence. The older TestHasPeerHeader tags stay: hasPeerHeader has no non-test caller, so those two tags prove a helper table only.

RFC7854-x-4.note: Re-judged 2026-09-29. rfc7854_wire_header_test.go::TestRFC7854PeerASIsFourOctetsWithTheShortASZeroPadded writes a Peer Down (writePeerHeader) into a patterned buffer and reads per-peer octets 26-29 raw: 65001 must be 00 00 FD E9 (the 16 most significant bits zero) and 4200000001 must be FA 56 EA 01, so a 2-octet field, a lost padding or a misplaced AS goes red. {single-polarity: positive} holds: the field is a fixed 4-octet encode with no shorter variant to refuse.

RFC7854-x-5.note: IPv4 lands in octets 12..15 with 0..11 zero; the IPv6 negative keeps its full address

RFC7854-x-6.note: collector reads the first message off a live TCP connection and asserts type Initiation; single-polarity marker

RFC7854-x-7.note: live Initiation carries sysName equal to the system identity and a sysDescr; single-polarity marker

RFC7854-x-8.note: Peer Up echoes both cached OPENs byte for byte (sender and event paths); with no cached OPENs no Peer Up is sent at all

RFC7854-x-9.note: Route Monitoring wraps the body in a full RFC 4271 header of type UPDATE; single-polarity marker
